title: Pinned USGS liquefaction code adds an unsquared standard deviation to its variance
abstract: We audit the general Zhu 2017 liquefaction routines in pinned public USGS ground-failure source. Both full and slim routines add the input model standard deviation to its square when forming a variance. All 560 controlled source-method tests reproduce this term. Changing one assignment restores the standard first-order rule. With fallback model SD 0.05, output SD is 4.58 times the standard value at zero shaking uncertainty and 1.63 times it at shaking log-SD 0.5. When both input SDs decrease together, source output SD decreases as the square root of the noise multiplier instead of linearly. An exact Gaussian reference confirms this limiting error. In a separate null result, all 85,316 selected cells in six paired archived liquefaction maps pass the bounded-variance test that some landslide maps failed. All 876,031 finite positive paired cells also pass. These maps do not identify separate input error components or the deployed executable. We establish a source-code discrepancy and a tested one-line repair, not an observed forecast calibration improvement. Code, aggregate evidence, exact hashes and external retrieval instructions are included.

display.caption: The source variance term raises output SD and fails the small-error limit. Six archived maps pass a separate necessary support test.

citations.reason: Supplies the six fixed event and release selections and the paired-product support-test question.
Selected work motivates a source-level audit of another public uncertainty product.
